claims.text: The prompt-engineered base GPT-4o-mini model achieved 58.7% accuracy on the held-out test split.
The fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini model achieved 88.6% accuracy on the held-out test split.

The domain-specific classifier (support vector machine over symptom-informed lexical features) achieved 91.9% accuracy (95% CI 91.4%-92.4%), exceeding both the base and fine-tuned large language models.
Soft probability fusion of the domain-specific classifier and fine-tuned large language model reached 93.9% accuracy (95% CI 93.5%-94.3%) at a 60% classifier to 40% fine-tuned model weighting.
Hybrid probability-indicator fusion reached 93.8% accuracy (95% CI 93.4%-94.2%) at a 60% classifier to 40% fine-tuned model weighting.
Both ensemble models significantly outperformed the domain-specific classifier alone (P < .001).
The accuracy of the soft fusion ensemble did not differ significantly from the hybrid fusion ensemble (P = .16).
The hybrid ensemble reduced the miss rate for the suicidal ideation category from 32.5% (650/2000) to 1.9% (37/2000) relative to the base model.
The advantage of the hybrid ensemble over the domain-specific classifier alone within the suicidal ideation category was not statistically significant (P = .68).
Ensemble accuracy fell discontinuously above a 50% language model weight, where the hybrid ensemble reduced exactly to the fine-tuned model.
General-purpose large language models can fail to recognize naturalistic text expressing suicidal ideation.

evidence.description: Base large language models achieved 58.7% accuracy on the test set of 12,178 posts.
Fine-tuned large language models achieved 88.6% accuracy on the held-out test split.
The domain-specific classifier achieved 91.9% accuracy (95% CI 91.4%-92.4%), exceeding the base (58.7%) and fine-tuned (88.6%) large language models.
Soft fusion reached 93.9% (95% CI 93.5%-94.3%) at a weighting of 60% classifier to 40% fine-tuned model.
Hybrid fusion reached 93.8% (95% CI 93.4%-94.2%) at a weighting of 60% classifier to 40% fine-tuned model.
P < .001 for both ensembles against the classifier alone based on exact McNemar tests.
The 2 ensembles did not differ from each other (P = .16) using exact McNemar tests.
The hybrid ensemble reduced the miss rate for the suicidal ideation category from 32.5% (650/2000) to 1.9% (37/2000), a 17.6-fold reduction relative to the base model.
The hybrid ensemble's advantage over the classifier alone within the suicidal ideation category was not significant (P = .68).

Accuracy fell discontinuously above a 50% language model weight, where the hybrid ensemble reduced exactly to the fine-tuned model; the selected weight satisfies the derived instance-level bound of 44.0%.
Base GPT-4o-mini had a miss rate of 32.5% (650/2000) for the suicidal ideation category.

methodologies.name: Domain-Specific NLP Classifier
methodologies.description: A support vector machine trained over symptom-informed lexical features to classify mental health-related text into 9 categories.
datasets: Reddit and Twitter mental health dataset (n=60,889)

methodologies.name: Hybrid Probability-Indicator Fusion Ensemble
methodologies.description: An ensemble combining predictions from a domain-specific classifier and fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini using probability-indicator fusion under derived closed-form weight bounds.
datasets: Reddit and Twitter mental health dataset (n=60,889)

methodologies.name: Soft Probability Fusion Ensemble
methodologies.description: An ensemble combining soft probabilities from a domain-specific classifier and fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini under closed-form weighting constraints.
datasets: Reddit and Twitter mental health dataset (n=60,889)

limitations.text: Labels were derived from the originating subreddit or a self-stated condition and are not clinical diagnoses.
Only one corpus was analyzed, limiting generalizability.
Ensembles integrating domain-specific natural language processing methods with large language models have not been formally characterized.

future_work.text: External validation on clinically characterized data before use in decision support.
